purpose: Native macOS terminal IDE for running many Claude Code sessions at once: tiling panes backed by a real tmux server, a backlog-driven left sidebar, browser panes, CVR launcher, and iPad remote access via Blink/mosh.
features: Tiling panes in rows, columns, or any nested combination; add/delete/resize freely
Real tmux under the hood: one tmux session per workspace, one window per pane; sessions survive app crashes and restarts
Claude Code awareness: per-pane status (working / needs input / done) via Claude Code hooks, notifications for unfocused panes
Project-level isolation: each Claude pane runs in its own folder with its own session/context/MCP
Native shell panes (zsh) alongside Claude panes
Browser panes (WKWebView) dockable anywhere; CVR recording launcher with optional window docking
Backlog left sidebar: full board from ~/.claude/backlog with per-workspace filters, search, detail view, status changes, create/edit, and Start->Claude pane
Workspaces -> tabs -> panes, with per-workspace base repo and persisted layouts
Mac-native keybindings plus tmux Ctrl+B prefix inside panes
iPad remote access: attach to any workspace from Blink Shell via mosh/ssh; bw companion CLI; Claude status in tmux status bar; mobile-tuned tmux defaults; Tailscale-aware connect strings

users.description: Single power user (the developer) on macOS; no multi-user, no auth

stack.database: none (JSON state file + markdown backlog files)

ai_features.description: Buildwright hosts Claude Code as terminal processes; it does not call any LLM APIs itself.

special_features: tmux topology: session name == workspace slug on the DEFAULT tmux socket so iPad attach is plain `tmux attach -t <workspace>`; hidden grouped sessions (prefix _bw-) let the app display each window in its own UI pane
Shared-view sizing: window-size=latest + aggressive-resize (latest input wins)
Claude hooks: UserPromptSubmit->working, Notification->needs-input, Stop->done, written to ~/.local/state/buildwright/status/<pane-id>.json by Scripts/bw-hook
Notifications via osascript (works without app-bundle entitlements)
CVR integration: launches existing tool at /Users/rvance/Documents/GitHub/docai/tools/cvr via npx tsx record.ts

integrations.name: tmux
integrations.notes: spawn/attach/control via tmux CLI on default socket, tmux >= 3.2 required

integrations.name: Claude Code CLI
integrations.notes: spawned in panes; hooks report status back

integrations.name: backlog skill files
integrations.notes: ~/.claude/backlog markdown read/write, BOARD.md regeneration, format-compatible with /backlog skill

integrations.name: CVR
integrations.notes: launch recordings; CVR remains source of truth for bundles

deployment.target: local macOS app bundle (Scripts/bundle.sh), no cloud

skipped_guardrails.tier1_web_guardrails: Not a web app: no frontend/backend split, no HTTP API, no browser UI of its own
skipped_guardrails.oidc_auth_rbac: Single-user local desktop tool; macOS user account is the security boundary. No auth, roles, or permissions
skipped_guardrails.database_migrations_seed: No database; state is a JSON file plus the user's existing backlog markdown
skipped_guardrails.docker_compose_mock_services: Native Mac app; Docker would defeat the purpose (needs PTYs, tmux, GUI). No external services to mock
skipped_guardrails.datatable_theme_components: Web component standards do not apply to SwiftUI
skipped_guardrails.activity_logs_notifications_modules: Web-app observability stack replaced by a local debug log (os.Logger); user-facing notifications are macOS notifications
skipped_guardrails.ai_guardrails_nemo: App makes no LLM calls itself; Claude Code's own safety applies inside panes
